<Heading
  as={"h1"}
  className={"openapi__heading"}
  children={"Takes a backup of runtime data"}
></Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/backupRuntime"}
  context={"endpoint"}
></MethodEndpoint>

With continuous backups enabled the `backupId` parameter must be omitted, as it's generated by
the cluster based on the current time and any offset configured. Otherwise, the `backupId` parameter
is required to specify the id of the backup to be taken.

Without `physicalTenant` a backup is triggered for every physical tenant of the cluster. The
caller-supplied `backupId` is used for every tenant; when ids are generated, each tenant gets
its own and `backupIds` maps every tenant to the id it was given.

The `physicalTenant` query parameter is only read when the request carries a
`Content-Type: application/json` header (the body itself may be empty). A request without
that header always covers every physical tenant.

If some tenants' backups are triggered and others fail, the status code is the failure's but
the body is still a `TakeBackupRuntimeResponse`: `backupIds` lists the backups that _were_
triggered so they can be monitored or deleted, and `failureReason` says what went wrong. It
also repeats the failure in `message`, so a client that reads error bodies as `Error` still
surfaces it.

<ParamsDetails
  parameters={[
    {
      name: "physicalTenant",
      required: false,
      in: "query",
      description:
        "Narrows the operation to the given physical tenant. When omitted, the operation covers every\nphysical tenant of the cluster, which on a single-tenant cluster is the one `default` tenant\nand therefore unchanged behavior.\n",
      schema: {
        title: "Physical Tenant ID",
        description:
          "The id of a physical tenant, as configured under `camunda.physical-tenants`. A cluster that\nconfigures none has exactly one physical tenant, `default`.\n",
        type: "string",
        example: "tenanta",
      },
    },
  ]}
></ParamsDetails>

<RequestSchema
  title={"Body"}
  body={{
    required: false,
    content: {
      "application/json": {
        schema: {
          title: "TakeBackupRequest",
          description: "Request body for take backup",
          type: "object",
          required: ["backupId"],
          properties: {
            backupId: {
              description: "The ID of the backup to be taken",
              allOf: [
                {
                  title: "Backup ID",
                  description:
                    "The ID of the backup. The ID of the backup must be a positive numerical value. As backups\nare logically ordered by their IDs (ascending), each successive backup must use a higher\nID than the previous one.\n",
                  type: "integer",
                  format: "int64",
                  example: 1,
                  minimum: 0,
                },
              ],
            },
          },
        },
      },
    },
  }}
></RequestSchema>

<StatusCodes
  id={undefined}

  responses={{
    "202": {

      content: {

            type: "object",
            properties: {
              backupId: {
                description:

              backupIds: {
